features.headline: NFL offseason free agent and trade acquisitions that have and have not worked
features.desc: Kenneth Walker III and Devin Lloyd look great with their new teams in 2026. But Jaylen Waddle and Alontae Taylor haven't quite found their groove.
body: Everyone loves the NFL offseason hot stove. Fans get super excited about outside players joining their favorite team, whether through trade or free agency. Those holes on the roster have finally been filled by wily veterans!

Unfortunately, those moves don't always work out. Some players excel in new surroundings, bringing strong production. Others struggle with their new situation, confirming why they were made available in the first place.

Here's a look at five players who are working well with their new teams and five who are not. How are the successful new players helping their teams? Which teams find themselves on the hook for bad contracts? Let's start with a quarterback who has helped two teams this season.
Jump to a section: Moves that have worked out Moves that have not yet worked out

How he got there: Signed a one-year, $11.3 million contract with the Raiders before being traded to the Vikings on Nov. 10 2026 stat to know: 65.0 QBR (10th out of 31 qualifying QBs) Comparable 2025 stat: 47.6 QBR (not enough passes to qualify)

This is a bit of a special case, because Cousins is thriving in his second new city of the season. Or perhaps we should say one new and one old city, because Cousins played for Minnesota from 2018 to 2023.
His performance this season is further proof that it takes a long time to recover from an Achilles tear. Cousins tore his Achilles in 2023 on the last play of his previous stint with the Vikings.

He went to Atlanta in 2024 and was completely immobile on plays such as rollouts and play-action fakes. He put up a career-low QBR of 47.0 and lost the starting job to then-rookie Michael Penix Jr. toward the end of the season.

features.headline: With Titans, Eagles up next, it's now or never for Cowboys
features.desc: Thanks to the scuffling NFC East and a friendly schedule the next week, the Cowboys still have a playoff shot.
body: FRISCO, Texas — The fate of the Dallas Cowboys' season will come into focus over the next two games.
Beat the Tennessee Titans on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox) and the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving, and the Cowboys (4-6) will have a path forward to potentially winning the NFC East.
Split the games, and they will need even more help from the division-leading New York Giants (5-3-1). Lose both and it could be time to ponder more changes to the coaching staff.

The math might still work with either of the last two options, but it would strain credulity if the Cowboys are unable to beat the one-win Titans and the two-win Eagles — with ESPN's FPI currently giving Dallas a 42.9% chance to reach the postseason.

Coach Brian Schottenheimer acknowledged Wednesday, when confirming the news that senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine would take over playcalling duties from coordinator Christian Parker, that the season would be a failure if the Cowboys don't make the playoffs.
He was asked, in extension of that comment, if the season is on the line in the next two games.
"I think they're very important games," Schottenheimer said. "Yes, I do."
It's not quite former Cowboys coach Jimmy Johnson's "We will win the game. Put it in three-inch headlines" statement prior to the 1993 NFC Championship Game.

It's not former Giants coach Jim Fassel with his team at 7-4 and having lost two straight, saying, "This is a poker game, and I'm shoving my chips to the middle of the table. I'm raising the ante.... This team is going to the playoffs."

features.headline: How Bhayshul Tuten became the clear No. 1 running back for the Jaguars
features.desc: After a lackluster rookie season, Tuten ranks 14th in NFL in rushing yards entering Sunday's game against the Giants.
body: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — In the offseason, no one was completely sure if Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten could replace Travis Etienne Jr. as the Jaguars' lead back.
The team signed Chris Rodriguez Jr. (who played for coach Liam Coen at Kentucky) as a free agent to help with the loss of Etienne.
Fast forward 10 weeks into the 2026 season, and nobody's doubting whether Tuten can carry the Jaguars' run game now.
"We could see the glimpse of a true RB1, but he hasn't done it on that type of level yet for being that consistent for an entire year of being the guy" running backs coach Chad Morton said.

"So we were unsure about what he's going to be able to handle and [if he could] just figure everything out and deal with the whole playbook and just the consistency. Can he block? Can he catch passes?
"So that was always going to be a concern from him, but we knew that he had the ability to do it. It's just, can we bring him along enough to get him to that point?"
He's there. Entering Sunday's game against the New York Giants (4:25 p.m. ET, CBS), Tuten leads the Jaguars with 609 rushing yards and has accounted for 64% of the running back carries.
He's on pace for 1,150 yards, which would be 25 more than Etienne posted in any of his five seasons in Jacksonville. His 67.7 rushing yards per game ranks 12th in the NFL.

Tuten has also established himself as one of the league's toughest running backs to bring down, ranking seventh in rushing yards after first contact (360) and sixth in yards per rush after first contact (2.43).

features.headline: Messi vs. Ronaldo, Man Utd hire Moyes: GTA V came out in a different soccer world
features.desc: As Grand Theft Auto VI is finally unleashed, here is what was happening in the world of soccer when the previous game was released 13 years ago
body: Given that it's the only thing anybody appears to be talking about, you may be aware that a new video game by the name of "Grand Theft Auto VI" was released on Thursday, thus ending a long and arduous 13-year wait among fans of the infamous Rockstar Games franchise for a new instalment.
The previous game in the series, GTA V, was launched what feels like an eon ago during the primordial mists of September 2013. Almost a decade-and-a-half later, GTA VI is finally upon us.
We couldn't help but ponder just how the soccer landscape has changed during those intervening years — or not, as the case may be.

- Mr. Worldwide: Meet soccer star who's played for clubs on 6 continents - MrBeast, meet Haaland: Man City star puts YouTuber through gauntlet - Why Champions League's iconic 'star' match ball may soon be replaced
One thing which is the same as it was in 2013 is Spain's dominance over men's international competition.

On the release of GTA V, La Roja were reigning world and European champions after winning the UEFA European Championship in 2008 and 2012, either side of their triumph at the 2010 FIFA World Cup, in an unprecedented era of back-to-back-to-back glory.
Skip forward 13 years and Spain — inspired by the likes of Lamine Yamal — are back on top having emerged triumphant at both Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup.
And now Spain's women's team is along for the ride, too, winning the Women's World Cup in 2023 and heading into next year's tournament as favorites.
Excelling on either side of the Clásico divide, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo were at the peak of their respective powers in 2013 at Barcelona and Real Madrid respectively.

features.headline: Estêvão is Brazil's brightest young talent. Is Chelsea the right place for him?
features.desc: Estêvão is widely regarded as Brazil's brightest young talent, but he has struggled for playing time at Chelsea this season. What's behind his lack of minutes?
body: After one of Estêvão's matches for Palmeiras, coach Abel Ferreira could no longer hold back.
"He is different from anything else I've ever seen," he said.

It was a big claim. Ferreira had a long playing career in his native Portugal, and coached there and in Greece before heading to Brazil. And he was blown away not just by the talent of the youngster, but also by his work ethic and the strength of his temperament.
Ferreira went as far as to make a public appeal to the Palmeiras president to hang on to Estêvão, rather than transfer him as soon as he turned 18.

His plea, predictably, wasn't heeded and Estêvão signed off last year at the FIFA Club World Cup. His last act as a Palmeiras player was to score a wonder goal against Chelsea, the club he was about to join, thereby instantly winning the respect of his new teammates.

And, at a club with a tradition of exciting wingers, it did not take long for Estêvão to win the hearts of the Chelsea fanbase. So English soccer had, for the first time, a genuine Brazilian superstar in the making who had chosen the Premier League over the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

His debut European season was cut short by a serious hamstring injury that forced him out of the World Cup. But with eight goals in 36 games and plenty of magical moments along the way, it was a splendid return from his debut Premier League campaign.
Now, surely, it was a case of sit back and enjoy the show. Except that, so far, things have not worked out like that at all.
Estêvão has run into a common problem — the difficult second season. So far, he has been nothing more than a bit-part player. What has happened?

features.headline: Mauricio Pochettino's Man United squad audit: Should Fernandes, Rashford stay?
features.desc: New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino inherits a squad built by his six predecessors. Which players have a future at the club, and which should go?
body: Mauricio Pochettino has arrived at Manchester United and the former United States men's national team coach has no time to waste as the new manager of the Premier League's fallen giants.

Pochettino's immediate task is to halt the team's slump and drag United out of the relegation zone, starting with Sunday's trip to Liverpool as his first game in charge. Securing a first league win since August is also a priority for the former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea boss.
However, the 54-year-old must look beyond the short term at Old Trafford. He must begin to shape a team in his own image, with players capable of playing the Pochettino way.

- Man United, Pochettino's to-do list based on what's gone wrong - Pochettino can't fix United on his own. The owners have to do their jobs - Where are they now? Every Utd player, coach, exec since Glazers' takeover

Former United captain Gary Neville said last week that, while interviewing him at Spurs in 2014, Pochettino was sat in front of a whiteboard with two lists of players: those he could trust and build around, and those he decided he could not work with.

Having inherited a squad built by United's six previous managers dating back to Louis van Gaal's signing of Luke Shaw in 2014, Pochettino must quickly assess his players and draw up a similar list of who will stay and who will go.
So with the Pochettino era about to start at United, what will his whiteboard look like at the end of the season? Who stays, and who has to go?
